source_contract: fixed MoviePilot app/core/plugin.py:156 stop and :619 __stop_plugin/:641 reload
Go process adapter owns bounded cancellation/cleanup; successful stop must not turn into a late canceled-phase pipe error
root_cause: Cancellation sender checked live under manager mutex before waiting on transport.writeMu. Stop could then fence/serialize its final cleanup and worker exit before the queued cancellation reached the pipe. Its stale write failed, aborting the entire session and converting successful cleanup to worker_io_failed. Actual temporary stack diagnosis shows failing iterations first abort at callStarted cancellation goroutine, not reader EOF.
diagnostic_red: Temporary stack-only host diagnostic added to abort then removed; separate50-repeat normal worker/host-race run failed3/pass47; preexisting root100-repeat run failed14/pass86 retained separately. No diagnosis logs entered product.
fix: The manager liveness check now executes as the cancellation write charge callback while transport.writeMu is held. Stop/shutdown/completed phases suppress only that obsolete control notification before any byte is written; unrelated/live I/O errors still abort. Transport protocol, negotiated limits, admission and method authority unchanged.
causal_test: Hold actual writeMu, observe cancellation goroutine already queued in concurrentTransport.write via runtime.Stack (not a timing sleep), apply stop/shutdown/completed fence, release mutex. Assert zero physical writes/no terminal abort. A live cleanup notification under draining still writes and a real closed-pipe error remains terminal. No production test hook added.
mutation: Restore the exact old pre-lock live-check sequence within factored notifyCancellation via go overlay; all3 controlled fence cases fail with one real writer attempt/worker_io_failed. Current20 repetitions pass.
freeze: Product changes complete; coordinator independently reviewed charge lock order and is rebuilding final server/worker dependency closure. Only evidence will be amended after this point.
impact: Shared host SDK package input changed: old executable build manifests remain historical evidence. New final server and all acceptance workers must be rebuilt/resealed, then final platform/SDK/actual Linux/browser gates executed. No old acceptance SHA silently rewritten.
delivery: No commit/push/production deployment; no worker business or production endpoint touched.
